paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus goes looking for people, and He doesn't wait for them to clean up first. Zacchaeus was a chief tax collector, very wealthy, and the crowd had already made up its mind about him. They grumbled, "He has gone to be the guest of a sinful man!" (Luke 19:7). And Jesus went to his house anyway.

Now look at what happened to Zacchaeus after that. Jesus never handed him a list of rules. Zacchaeus stood up and said, "Look, Lord, half of my possessions I give to the poor, and if I have cheated anyone, I will repay it fourfold" (Luke 19:8). That's what being welcomed by Jesus does to a heart. The change came out of a joyful welcome, and Jesus said, "Today salvation has come to this house, because this man too is a son of Abraham" (Luke 19:9).

Here's why it matters to you, baker. Jesus said, "For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost" (Luke 19:10). I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and I can tell you that being sought out hits different than being stuck there. You don't have to fix yourself before He shows up, because He's already looking for you. So when you feel too small, too far back or too far gone, remember that Jesus looks up and says your NAME.
